###### ✦

Good morning, founders 🕶️

Two rules run through this edition: **whatever you reward gets farmed, and whatever you automate, you still own.** On Polymarket, a rumored token may have turned two finished election markets into $600M of volume. In New York, CarGurus is finding out that its chatbot's "deals" count as its own promises. And OpenAI just reminded everyone building on GPT-4o that a model is a lease, not a purchase. 

Three stories, one blind spot: an incentive or a dependency nobody was watching. Which number on your dashboard would survive two accounts trading with each other?

In today's newsletter, we'll get into:

* Polymarket's $600M zombie election markets

* NYC sues CarGurus over its chatbot's "deals"

* OpenAI puts GPT-4o on a 92-day clock

* Bluesky wants payments across every app

----------
* 🔌 An OpenAI engineer was charged after allegedly hiding a thumb-drive-sized recorder in the USB port behind a conference-room TV. [Spend five minutes checking the ports behind your screens](https://www.inc.com/kit-eaton/an-alleged-spy-device-was-hidden-at-openai-check-this-overlooked-spot-in-your-office-today/91420378).

* 🧑‍🔧 US forward-deployed engineer postings jumped from under 200 in 2023 to 7,300+ this year (Lightcast). Selling AI to enterprises? [Budget for an embedded engineer](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/aws-anthropic-racing-to-deploy-army-of-specialized-ai-engineers.html); median ads hit $195K.

* 🕵️ 82% of organizations found AI agents they didn't know about (Cloud Security Alliance). [List every agent touching your email and storage](https://www.fastcompany.com/91623134/ai-agents-work-employees-risks), then write a permissions policy.

* ⏳ If engineers write code 4x faster but it waits in the same queues, nothing got faster, argues Precisely's CEO. [Cut approval steps before buying more AI tools](https://thenewstack.io/becoming-an-ai-company/).

* 🛂 Self-sponsoring a US visa? USCIS needs someone who can fire you, and your spouse won't count. [Seat an independent board with real firing authority](https://www.entrepreneur.com/building-a-business/want-to-self-sponsor-your-u-s-visa-avoid-these-3-common-governance-mistakes) at formation, not filing.

## Five bullets of updates

1. 🚗 **New York City sued CarGurus, alleging 2,000+ consumer-law violations, including "Great Deal" badges and an AI chatbot listing "deals" that hid mandatory fees.** One Honda billed as $2,212 under market came out $1,473 over. The city's AI policy treats chatbot claims as the company's own, so [check what your bot promises against your real prices](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/news/71-26/mamdani-administration-sues-cargurus-deceiving-new-yorkers-ai-chatbot-hidden-junk-fees).

2. ⌚ **Withings now requires new accounts to pay $99.99 a year for Withings+ to auto-sync data to Apple Health, while accounts created on or before October 12 keep it free.** The grandfathering was real, but customers learned about it from a forum reply under a post titled "Unacceptable." Changing what's free? [Announce who's protected on day one](https://support.withings.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/51887047154577-Unacceptable-Apple-Health-Sync-is-now-behind-a-99-year-paywall-for-new-accounts), not in the comments.

3. ⚖️ **Chariot raised a $10M Series A led by Silverton Partners to help consumers file mass-arbitration claims over hidden fees, privacy violations and hard-to-cancel subscriptions.** The 15-person startup says it's breaking even on 200,000+ claim submissions a month. Your no-class-action clause doesn't stop claims. It turns one lawsuit into thousands, so [fix your cancel flow](https://news.crunchbase.com/ai/legal-tech-chariot-raise-stop-hidden-fees-subscriptions-hang/) before someone files over it.

4. 💳 **Ramp raised $1.85B at a $60B valuation, four months after raising $750M at $44B, with annualized revenue past $2B.** Investor Keith Rabois told TechCrunch he wants Ramp "more important than Anthropic" by owning how companies manage token spend. When your category commoditizes, [chase the next budget line your customers can't track](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/15/ramp-reaches-60b-valuation-as-it-pushes-deeper-into-ai/).

5. 🦋 **Bluesky plans to launch payments in the coming months for buying, selling and fundraising, meant to work across every app on its network, not just its own.** CEO Toni Schneider and COO Rose Wang pitched it at TechCrunch Disrupt as the first step toward making money without ads. Building on that network? [A shared payments rail](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/15/bluesky-wants-to-make-it-easier-to-buy-sell-and-fundraise-on-the-network/) could let your app charge users without building checkout from scratch.

### **$41M on the wrong guy: inside Polymarket's zombie election markets**

View image: (https://media1.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTI0NTBlYzMwZ3UwbzUyeHZxZzU5dWF4azBvNWEyaXdldWpuNnV2Z3NrcHNzMHNvYSZlcD12MV9naWZzX3NlYXJjaCZjdD1n/fBZP79EUciXAby8GJ0/giphy.gif) [Eyes Glow GIF by Adult Swim]
Follow image link: (https://startupclub.slidebean.com/)
Caption: Gif by adultswim on Giphy

This summer, Ethiopia's prime minister _Abiy Ahmed_ won in a landslide: **438** parliamentary seats to the runner-up's **13**. On _Polymarket_, traders put **$173,000** on him becoming the next leader, and more than **$41 million** on his chief of staff, _Shimelis Abdisa_. That's **200-plus times** more money on the man who didn't get the job.

**The receipt:** two election markets on Polymarket's offshore platform, Ethiopia and Romania, did **$600M+** in volume, mostly on long shots who lost. Of Ethiopia's **$285M+**, about **$284M** came from pairs of accounts trading with each other, says Chris Park, an ex-Polymarket trader who now runs forensics firm _MSR Decode_.

#### **Who trades a market that's already over?**

Not quants chasing pennies. MSR Decode traced **38,000+** "trade loops" after the vote, and **over 98%** ended with neither side up or down. Median hold: **nine seconds**. The market only resolved after the _October_ swearing-in, so it traded for _123 days_ after the election, a "zombie market" in economist Rajiv Sethi's words. Users asked: "THIS NOT RESOLVED?" In Romania, Sethi's algorithm flagged **99.6%** of some weeks' volume as wash trading.

#### **What were they farming?**

Probably a token that doesn't exist yet. In _2025_, Polymarket's CMO told a crypto podcast there "would be a token." If allocations reward volume, a zero-profit, nine-second round trip isn't bad trading. It's a job application. Wash trading breaks Polymarket's terms, and the company says it flagged the activity and blocked the accounts. Sethi's caveat: "What appears to be wash trading isn't always wash trading." Nobody knows who the traders are.

#### **Is your growth chart farmable?**

Whatever you reward with points, tokens, leaderboards or referral credits will get farmed, and the metric dies with it. Pick the number you'll pitch investors on and make sure two accounts can't fake it by trading with each other. Build self-dealing detection before launch, and shut down stale campaigns, promos and markets on schedule.

If a Polymarket token ever ships, its allocation rules will tell us what those nine seconds were worth.

Read the source (https://www.wired.com/story/over-dollar600-million-traded-on-polymarket-election-contracts-after-races-ended/)

### OpenAI just put your GPT-4o app on a 92-day clock

View image: (https://media1.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTI0NTBlYzMwajFteG5jNm92dTF3c3cwaGNvcXh5eTNmaHBhNnVzenlnZ2M3Zzg3aSZlcD12MV9naWZzX3NlYXJjaCZjdD1n/Qz4RaxcOh4qndWOG5N/giphy.gif) [Clock Tick Tock GIF by MOODMAN]
Follow image link: (https://startupclub.slidebean.com/)
Caption: Giphy

On _Wednesday, October 14_, OpenAI notified developers that _GPT-4o_, _GPT-4o mini_, _GPT-4.1_ and _GPT-4.1 mini_ leave the API on _January 14, 2027_. Every fine-tuned model built on them goes the same day. The recommended replacement for all four: _gpt-6-luna_.

That's **92 days**. OpenAI's own deprecations page promises generally available models **at least six months**, unless safety or compliance forces a faster timeline. The entry cites neither. Two weeks earlier, on the same page, _GPT-5.1_ got its full six months.

#### **Why panic now and not in December?**

Because the clock is shorter than it looks. Subtract the holidays and you have roughly ten working weeks. And swapping the model ID is the easy part: per **[The New Stack's read of the migration guide](https://thenewstack.io/openai-gpt4o-api-shutdown/)**, Luna only supports function calling in Chat Completions with reasoning switched off. Reasoning plus tool calls means moving to the Responses API.

#### **What does the countdown look like?**

* **This week:** grep your codebase for every 4o and 4.1 model ID, dated snapshots included.

* **By November:** run your evals on Luna. Not on OpenAI's Evals platform, though: existing evals go read-only _October 31_ and the whole thing shuts down _November 30_.

* **Before January 6:** that's when active customers lose the ability to start new fine-tuning jobs. If your moat is a fine-tune, rebuild it before then.

* **January 14:** lights out.

#### **So what's the founder takeaway?**

Treat any model like an apartment on a month-to-month lease. Put a routing layer between your product and the model, so the next deprecation email is a config change, not a fire drill. OpenAI says some customers can buy dedicated capacity to keep a model past shutdown. That's a sales call, not a plan.

Watch for pushback. 4o's fans got it back in ChatGPT once before, a day after GPT-5 replaced it.

Read the source (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
